successCriteria.description: approve deducts the request's inclusive day count (countLeaveDays) from the matched LeaveBalance via ILeaveBalanceRepository.deduct, inside the same IUnitOfWork transaction as the status update to APPROVED.

apply, approve, reject, and cancel each write an AuditLog record via IAuditService.record (entityType LEAVE_REQUEST; AuditAction.CREATE for apply, AuditAction.UPDATE for approve/reject/cancel) within the same transaction as the state change.
approve/reject/cancel enforce manager authorization: the actor must be the employee's manager (Employee.managerId === actorId) or have role HR_ADMIN, otherwise LeaveAuthorizationError is thrown.

apply verifies the employee exists with employmentStatus === 'ACTIVE' (via IEmployeeRepository.findById) and that an active LeavePolicy exists for the leave type (via ILeavePolicyRepository.findActiveByLeaveType), throwing InactiveEmployeeError and InactiveLeavePolicyError respectively.
Routes pass request.user.id and request.user.role as the actor to apply/approve/reject/cancel; the approve/reject body no longer supplies an approver identity (no approvedBy spoofing vector).
LeaveAuthorizationError, InactiveEmployeeError, and InactiveLeavePolicyError are exported from src/modules/leave/index.ts and used by the service.

tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.spec.ts is updated to construct LeaveService with the new dependencies (employee, policy, audit) and actor-based signatures, and adds coverage for deduction, audit writes, authorization, and apply-time checks; the suite passes.

constraints: The service owns the unit of work: all mutating operations (apply, approve, reject, cancel) run through the injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction and pass the transaction client as the optional LAST parameter to every participating repository/service call (leaveRequests, balances.deduct, audit.record, employee/policy reads). The service never imports the pool or a pg client directly.

LeaveService must depend on the other modules only through their public barrels (index.ts): IEmployeeRepository, ILeavePolicyRepository, IAuditService, ILeaveBalanceRepository. No import of another module's internals.

The actor identity and role come from the authenticated request.user (id + role), never from the request body. RBAC remains enforced by the route-level requireRole guard; the manager-relationship check is a service-level authorization rule.

The existing lifecycle, sufficiency, and overlap rules are preserved unchanged: PENDING -> APPROVED|REJECTED, PENDING|APPROVED -> CANCELLED; approve still enforces n <= availableDays and no overlapping APPROVED leave; countLeaveDays is the single day-count source.

The new typed errors (LeaveAuthorizationError, InactiveEmployeeError, InactiveLeavePolicyError) must be mapped to an HTTP error response (no unhandled rejections, GP-006); the code agent chooses the status/code consistent with the existing leave error mapping.
outOfScope: Notification creation on approve/reject (the reconciled architecture lists it, but this phase's gate findings do not require it and no INotificationService dependency is mandated).
Cancel restoring previously deducted days (restore on cancel of an APPROVED request) — not raised by the gate findings and not required by this phase.

Resolving the balance by leave_type + is_active (the canonical decision) instead of the existing policyId === leaveTypeId match — the balance-resolution divergence is not part of the four gate findings.
Adding audit writes to the balance module (BalanceService.deduct/restore/create) — a separate documented divergence, not in this phase's scope.

entityInvariants.invariant: A request may only be created (apply) when its employee's employmentStatus is ACTIVE and an active LeavePolicy exists for its leaveTypeId; approving it atomically deducts its inclusive day count from the matched LeaveBalance and writes an audit record; approve/reject/cancel require the actor to be the employee's manager or HR_ADMIN.

usedDays and remainingDays are mutated only through ILeaveBalanceRepository.deduct/restore within the leave approval transaction; the stored counters remain non-negative (NegativeBalanceCounterError on violation).
Every state-changing leave operation (apply/approve/reject/cancel) produces exactly one AuditLog record with entityType LEAVE_REQUEST, joined to the same transaction as the state change.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Caller must be authenticated (EMPLOYEE/MANAGER/HR_ADMIN); the employee referenced by input.employeeId must be ACTIVE and an active LeavePolicy must exist for the leave type.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: InactiveEmployeeError when employmentStatus !== ACTIVE; InactiveLeavePolicyError when no active policy for the leave type.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: actorRole must be HR_ADMIN, or actorId must equal the request employee's managerId; otherwise LeaveAuthorizationError.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: LeaveAuthorizationError on unauthorized actor; InvalidLeaveRequestTransitionError on non-PENDING; InsufficientLeaveBalanceError/OverlappingLeaveError preserved; null when the request does not exist.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: actorRole must be HR_ADMIN, or actorId must equal the request employee's managerId; otherwise LeaveAuthorizationError.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: LeaveAuthorizationError on unauthorized actor; InvalidLeaveRequestTransitionError on non-PENDING; null when the request does not exist.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: actorRole must be HR_ADMIN, or actorId must equal the request employee's managerId; otherwise LeaveAuthorizationError.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: LeaveAuthorizationError on unauthorized actor; InvalidLeaveRequestTransitionError on non-(PENDING|APPROVED); null when the request does not exist.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service must implement the actor-based signatures already declared in ILeaveService (apply/approve/reject/cancel take actorId + actorRole) and use the three error types already declared in leave.model.ts.

Balance deduction must go through ILeaveBalanceRepository.deduct(id, days, client) with the optional client as the LAST parameter, matching the declared signature and the NegativeBalanceCounterError contract.

Audit writes must go through IAuditService.record(input, client) with AuditAction.CREATE/UPDATE and EntityType.LEAVE_REQUEST, matching the declared AuditRecordInput shape and the optional-client join contract.
Employee lookup must use IEmployeeRepository.findById and read Employee.employmentStatus/managerId with the exact field names declared in the employee model.
Policy resolution must use ILeavePolicyRepository.findActiveByLeaveType(leaveType, client) and read LeavePolicy.isActive, matching the declared signature.
The transaction boundary must follow the IUnitOfWork.withTransaction contract and the AGENTS.md rule 5 pattern (service owns the boundary, data-access opens it, client passed as optional last param).

integrationPoints.why: apply-time ACTIVE check and approve/reject/cancel manager-relationship check require reading Employee.employmentStatus and Employee.managerId.
apply-time active-policy check requires findActiveByLeaveType for the request's leave type.
GP-002 requires an audit record for every state-changing leave operation, joined to the caller's transaction.
approve must deduct the inclusive day count atomically with the status change.
